tower-of-hanoi.title: Move largest needed disk first if not on target
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Identify the largest disk that is not already on its goal peg, and move it directly to its goal before handling any smaller disks.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When the current configuration has the largest needed disk on a different peg than its goal.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move a smaller disk while a larger needed disk remains on a different peg, causing the larger disk to stay misplaced.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Recursively solve remaining disks after placing largest
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After placing the largest needed disk on its goal peg, treat the remaining smaller disks as a new subproblem and solve it using the same strategy.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Immediately after the largest needed disk has been correctly positioned.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Continuing to move smaller disks without first fixing the position of the largest needed disk, leading to extra moves.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Standard recursive transfer of k disks
tower-of-hanoi.principle: To move a stack of k disks from a source peg to a target peg, first recursively move the top k‑1 disks to the auxiliary peg, then move the kth (largest) disk to the target, and finally move the k‑1 disks from the auxiliary to the target.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need to transfer a contiguous stack of disks between two pegs.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Trying to move the largest disk of a stack while smaller disks are still on top of it, violating the rule that only the topmost disk may be moved.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Output move list as final parseable block
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The response must end with a single, syntactically correct list of moves in bracket notation; any trailing text will be ignored by the parser.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Appending explanatory text after the move list, so the parser reads only the text and misses the moves.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Verify final configuration before output
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After constructing the move list, mentally replay each move from the initial state to ensure the final arrangement matches the goal exactly.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Submitting a move sequence that leaves a disk on the wrong peg, resulting in a final configuration that does not match the goal.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Provide only the move list, no extra text
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The response should contain just the move list and nothing else (no explanations, duplicate lists, or surrounding narrative).
tower-of-hanoi.example: Including a preamble like 'Here is the solution:' before the move list, causing the parser to fail to extract the list.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate legality of each move
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Before adding a move, check that the chosen disk is the topmost on its source peg and that the destination peg does not have a smaller disk on top.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: During construction of the move sequence.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving a disk that is buried under another disk on its source peg, which is illegal.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Clear target peg of smaller disks before moving larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Never place a larger disk onto a peg that currently holds any smaller disk; first relocate those smaller disks to another peg.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Before moving a larger disk onto a peg that already contains disks.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Placing a larger disk onto a peg where a smaller disk sits on top, breaking the size rule.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Avoid moving small disks onto a peg that will later receive a larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Do not place a small disk onto a peg if a larger disk still needs to be moved onto that same peg later, as it will block the larger disk.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When deciding where to temporarily store a small disk.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving the smallest disk onto the final target peg early, then later trying to place a larger disk onto that peg, which becomes impossible.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Move blocking smaller disks to any other peg (auxiliary or target) before moving larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If a larger disk is blocked by smaller disks on its source peg, relocate those smaller disks to any other peg—either the auxiliary peg or the target peg (provided the target’s top disk is larger)—so the larger disk can be moved.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When a larger disk is not topmost because smaller disks sit on it.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Leaving a smaller disk on the source peg and attempting to move the larger disk underneath it, resulting in an illegal move.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may assume no moves are needed or forget to output the required list.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always generate a move list, even if it is empty, and ensure it is included in the response.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model runs out of tokens or stops generation prematurely.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Plan the full sequence before output and verify that the list ends with a closing bracket.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Attempted to move a disk that is not the topmost on its source peg
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model loses track of the stack order while planning moves.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Before each move, check that the chosen disk is the topmost on its current peg.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Prematurely moving a smaller disk onto the final target peg, causing later moves to be impossible
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model treats the target peg as a convenient temporary location without considering future larger‑disk placements.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Keep the final target peg free of smaller disks until all larger disks have been placed there.
